summary: Credential handoff encoding error: GCP->AWS session tags truncated during ephemeral env bootstrap
description:
Issue summary:
During ephemeral environment provisioning (ephemeral-llm-debug) the internal credential broker fails to hand off short-lived AWS credentials derived from GCP Workload Identity Federation. The STS AssumeRole call succeeds but session tags sent by the broker are being truncated or dropped, leading to downstream auth/authorization failures and policy mismatches when the provisioner attempts to access dedicated account resources.

Impact:
- Self-service ephemeral sandboxes for ML/debugging are failing for ~30% of requests in eu-west (partial failure pattern).
- Engineers are blocked from reproducing production issues using ephemeral infra; provisioning falls back to manual escalation which increases support load.
- Potential security gap: incorrectly-tagged sessions bypass some scoping checks, increasing blast radius risk if not contained.

Environment:
- Production credential broker (credentials-broker v2.3.1)
- Provisioner service (provisioner v1.8.0)
- GCP Workload Identity Provider -> AWS STS AssumeRole chain
- Observed mostly in eu-west-1 control plane; sporadic in us-east-1

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger ephemeral env bootstrap from console or infra CLI with a user that is allowed to federate from GCP project:redwood-ephemeral.
2) Broker exchanges GCP token for AWS STS credentials and attaches session tags (org, env, request_id, engineer_email).
3) Provisioner uses those credentials to call account APIs (create role bindings, attach kms keys).
4) Calls fail with access denied OR resource policies evaluate differently.

Observed behavior:
- STS:AssumeRole returns credentials but CloudTrail shows sessionContext attributes with truncated tag values (e.g., request_id becomes "req-..." or engineer_email omitted).
- Provisioner logs: "authorization: tag mismatch for resource write" or "policy evaluation returned DENY due to missing tag 'env'".
- Correlation: failures line up with credential-broker instances upgraded two weeks ago from go-uuid v1 to v2 (internal encoding change).

Expected behavior:
- Broker should preserve full UTF-8 tag values; AWS STS session tags must arrive intact for policy evaluation.

Relevant logs & traces:
- Provisioner trace: trace-id p-7a2b3c -> https://observability.redwood/trace/p-7a2b3c
- Broker request: request-id cb-9f8e7d -> https://observability.redwood/logs/cb-9f8e7d
- CloudTrail snippets: show SessionTags field with truncated strings for affected sessions. Attached sample snippets in runbook (Confluence).

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Rolled back credentials-broker from v2.3.1 -> v2.2.6 for eu-west fleet (partial mitigation). New ephemeral requests routed to v2.2.6 and success rate improved to ~95% for a subset of users.
- Added provisional guard in provisioner to re-fetch tags from config metadata when missing (patch to tolerate missing tags, not a security fix).

Next steps (investigation/plan):
- Confirm encoding/path in broker that marshals tags into the AssumeRole request (suspect URL-encoding vs base64 path introduced in v2.3.1).
- Reproduce in a controlled lab with exact tag values including special characters (plus signs, colons, and long emails).
- Coordinate ACCT/SRE and Security to validate rollback and run long-tail audits for any sessions created with missing tags.
- Implement a hard validation check in broker to fail-fast if tag values would be truncated by the AWS API and add end-to-end test coverage.
- Prepare a forward-fix PR to normalize encoding and add a migration plan for staged rollout behind feature flag.

Priority justification:
- This issue affects developer productivity and may allow incorrectly-scoped sessions; needs P1/Sev1 attention and cross-team coordination.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: encoding/library change in credentials-broker v2.3.1 introduced URL-encoding of tag values; AWS STS expects raw UTF-8 or different percent-encoding semantics, causing truncation when '+' or ':' present.

Reproducer: created GCP WIF token with 'engineer_email=dev+infra@redwood.com' and long request_id length >128 chars. When broker used v2.3.1, CloudTrail showed truncated session tag; with v2.2.6 full value present.
Observed that AWS SDK wrapper in broker limits tag size or performs an unintended split when serializing to query parameters. Need to audit SDK usage and our wrapper code for custom escaping.
Mitigation effectiveness: rollback to v2.2.6 improved success rate from ~70% -> ~95% for incoming requests; remaining failures are from pre-warmed credentials and cached broker instances.
resolution: In progress. Temporary rollback to credentials-broker v2.2.6 applied for eu-west. Security policy tightened to deny actions if critical tags missing. Engineering to land encoding fix in credentials-broker and add e2e tests; plan staged rollout behind feature flag and monitor for 48 hours. Postmortem to be created after fix and rollout.
